responsibility: Provides rustc’s transmutability analysis crate: it defines the public API, assumptions, and result vocabulary for answering whether one type may be transmuted to another, and when compiled with rustc integration it exposes the compiler-facing entry points that translate rustc types and const-transmute options into internal queries. Its `layout` module supplies the shared type-layout model and conversion pipeline used by the analysis: `layout/mod.rs` defines the common abstractions and rustc adapters for extracting layouts and reference metadata, `layout/tree.rs` constructs and prunes tree-shaped layouts that capture bytes, references, definitions, sequencing, alternation, and inhabitedness, `layout/tree/tests.rs` validates those pruning rules, `layout/nfa.rs` lowers pruned trees into nondeterministic automata over byte offsets and validity/reference edges, and `layout/dfa.rs` determinizes them into transition tables suitable for comparison. Its internal `maybe_transmutable` module implements the generic decision procedure that runs `MaybeTransmutableQuery` over those layout representations to produce `Answer` and `Reason` outcomes, with `maybe_transmutable/query_context.rs` defining the abstract and concrete context interface that supplies environment-specific layout components and `maybe_transmutable/tests.rs` specifying end-to-end behavior across safety and validity cases. Together, the crate turns compiler type layout information into a reusable, assumption-aware check of whether a proposed transmute is permitted and why.
